paras.uz: U og'ir, g'ichirlaydigan, shaffof bo'lmagan eshikni ochdi va biz qorong'i, tartibsiz bir bo'shliqda (ular buni «kvartira» deb atashgan) o'zimizni topdik. O'sha g'alati «qirollik» cholg'usi va xuddi ularning qadimiy musiqasidek ranglar va shakllarning yovvoyi, uyushmagan, telba baqiroqligi. Tepada oq tekislik, to'q moviy devorlar, qadimiy kitoblarning qizil, yashil, to'q sariq muqovalari, sariq bronza shamdonlar, Budda haykali, epilepsiyadan buzilgan chiziqli, hech qanday aniq tenglamaga keltirib bo'lmaydigan mebel.

paras.en: I could hardly bear that chaos. But my companion apparently possessed a stronger constitution.
paras.uz: Men bu tartibsizlikka zo'rg'a chiday olardim. Lekin hamrohimning tuzilishi, aftidan, mustahkamroq edi.

paras.en: “This is my most beloved⁠—” she suddenly caught herself (again a smile⁠—bite, and white sharp teeth), “to be more exact, the most nonsensical of all ‘apartments.’ ”
paras.uz: «Bu mening eng sevimli...» — u to'satdan o'zini tutib oldi (yana tabassum-tishlash va oq o'tkir tishlar), — aniqrog'i, barcha "kvartira"larning eng bema'nisi».

paras.en: “Or to be most exact, of all the States. Thousands of microscopic States, fighting eternal wars, pitiless like⁠—”
paras.uz: «Yoki eng aniqrog'i, barcha davlatlarning. Abadiy urushlar olib boradigan, shafqatsiz minglab mikroskopik davlatlar...»

paras.en: “Oh yes, it’s clear,” said I-330 with apparent sincerity.
paras.uz: «Oh, ha, aniq», — dedi I-330 ko'rinishdan samimiy.

paras.en: We passed through a room where we found a few small children’s beds (children in those days were also private property). Then more rooms, glimmering mirrors, sombre closets, unbearably loud-colored divans, an enormous “fireplace,” a large mahogany bed. Our contemporary beautiful, transparent, eternal glass was represented here only by pitiful, delicate, tiny squares of windows.
paras.uz: Biz bir nechta kichkina bolalar karavoti bor xonadan o'tdik (o'sha kunlarda bolalar ham xususiy mulk edi). Keyin yana xonalar, yaltirayotgan ko'zgular, qorong'i shkaflar, chidab bo'lmas darajada baqiroq rangli divanlar, ulkan «kamin», katta qizil daraxt karavot. Bizning zamonaviy go'zal, shaffof, abadiy shishamiz bu yerda faqat ayanchli, nozik, mitti derazalar kvadratchalari bilan ifodalangan edi.

paras.en: “And to think; here there was love ‘just so’; they burned and tortured themselves” (again the curtain of the eyes was lowered), “What a stupid, uneconomical spending of human energy. Am I not right?”
paras.uz: «O'ylab ko'ring: bu yerda "shunchaki" sevishgan; yonishgan va o'zlarini qiynashgan» (yana ko'zlar pardasi tushdi). «Inson energiyasining qanday ahmoqona, tejamsiz sarflanishi. To'g'ri emasmi?»

paras.en: She spoke as though reading my thoughts but in her smile there remained always that irritating X. There behind the curtains something was going on, I don’t know what, but something that made me lose my patience. I wanted to quarrel with her, to scream at her (exactly, to scream), but I had to agree. It was impossible not to agree.
paras.uz: U go'yo fikrlarimni o'qiyotgandek gapirardi, lekin uning tabassumida doim o'sha g'ashga tegadigan X qolardi. U yerda, pardalar ortida nimadir bo'layotgan edi, nima ekanini bilmayman, lekin sabrimni yo'qotishimga sabab bo'lgan nimadir. Men u bilan janjallashmoqchi, unga baqirmoqchi edim (aynan baqirmoqchi), lekin rozi bo'lishim kerak edi. Rozi bo'lmaslik imkonsiz edi.

paras.en: We stopped in front of a mirror. At that moment I saw only her eyes. An idea came to me: human beings are built as nonsensically as these stupid “apartments,” human heads are opaque, and there are only two very small windows that lead inside⁠—the eyes. She seemed to have guessed my thoughts; she turned around: “Well, here they are, my eyes⁠—well” (this suddenly, then silence).
paras.uz: Biz ko'zgu oldida to'xtadik. O'sha lahzada men faqat uning ko'zlarini ko'rdim. Xayolimga bir fikr keldi: odamlar bu ahmoqona «kvartira»lar kabi bema'ni qurilgan, odam boshlari shaffof emas va ichkariga olib boradigan faqat ikkita juda kichik deraza bor — ko'zlar. U fikrlarimni taxmin qilganday bo'ldi; o'girildi: «Mana, ular, mening ko'zlarim — xo'sh» (bu to'satdan, keyin sukut).

paras.en: There were in front of me two gloomy dark windows and behind them inside, such strange hidden life. I saw there only fire, burning like a peculiar “fireplace” and unknown figures resembling.⁠ ⁠…
paras.uz: Oldimda ikkita g'amgin qorong'i deraza bor edi, ularning ortida, ichkarida esa shunday g'alati yashirin hayot. Men u yerda faqat olovni, o'ziga xos «kamin»dek yonayotgan olovni va qandaydir o'xshash noma'lum qiyofalarni ko'rdim...

paras.en: All this was certainly very natural; I saw in her eyes the reflection of my own face. But my feelings were unnatural and not like me. Evidently the depressing influence of the surroundings was beginning to tell on me. I felt definitely fear. I felt as if I were trapped and caged in a strange cage. I felt that I was caught in the wild hurricane of ancient life.
paras.uz: Bularning hammasi, albatta, juda tabiiy edi; men uning ko'zlarida o'z yuzimning aksini ko'rdim. Lekin tuyg'ularim g'ayritabiiy va menga o'xshamas edi. Aftidan, muhitning ezuvchi ta'siri menga ta'sir qila boshlagan edi. Men aniq qo'rquv his qildim. O'zimni tuzoqqa tushgandek, g'alati qafasga qamalgandek his qildim. O'zimni qadimiy hayotning yovvoyi bo'roniga tushib qolgandek his qildim.

paras.en: “Do you know⁠ ⁠…” said I-330, “step out for a moment into the next room.” Her voice came from there⁠—from inside, from behind the dark window-eyes⁠—where the fireplace was blazing.
paras.uz: «Bilasizmi... — dedi I-330, — bir lahzaga qo'shni xonaga chiqib turing». Uning ovozi u yerdan — ichkaridan, qorong'i ko'z-derazalar ortidan, kamin alangalanayotgan joydan kelardi.

paras.en: I went out, sat down. From a shelf on the wall there looked straight into my face, somewhat smiling, a snub-nosed, asymmetrical physiognomy of one of the ancient poets; I think it was Pushkin.
paras.uz: Men chiqib, o'tirdim. Devordagi tokchadan to'g'ri yuzimga biroz jilmayib qadimgi shoirlardan birining puchuq burunli, nosimmetrik qiyofasi qarab turardi; menimcha, bu Pushkin edi.

paras.en: “Why do I sit here enduring this smile with such resignation and what is this all about? Why am I here? And why all these strange sensations, this irritating, repellent female, this strange game?”
paras.uz: «Nega men bu yerda o'tirib, bu tabassumga shunchalik itoatkorlik bilan chidab o'tiribman va bularning hammasi nima? Nega men bu yerdaman? Va nega bu g'alati tuyg'ular, bu g'ashga tegadigan, itaruvchi ayol, bu g'alati o'yin?»

paras.en: The door of the closet slammed; there was the rustle of silk. I felt it difficult to restrain myself from getting up and, and.⁠ ⁠… I don’t remember exactly; probably I wanted to tell her a number of disagreeable things. But she had already appeared.
paras.uz: Shkafning eshigi tarsillab yopildi; ipakning shitirlashi eshitildi. Men o'rnimdan turib, va... tiyilishim qiyin edi. Aniq eslay olmayman; ehtimol, unga bir qancha yoqimsiz gaplar aytmoqchi bo'lgandirman. Lekin u allaqachon paydo bo'lgan edi.

paras.en: She was dressed in a short bright-yellowish dress, black hat, black stockings. The dress was of light silk⁠—I saw clearly very long black stockings above the knees, an uncovered neck and the shadow between.⁠ ⁠…
paras.uz: U qisqa, och sarg'ish ko'ylak, qora shlyapa, qora paypoq kiygan edi. Ko'ylak yengil ipakdan edi — men tizzadan yuqoridagi juda uzun qora paypoqlarni, ochiq bo'ynini va oradagi soyani aniq ko'rdim...

paras.en: “It’s clear that you want to seem original. But is it possible that you⁠—?”
paras.uz: «Aniqki, siz o'ziga xos ko'rinmoqchisiz. Lekin nahotki siz...?»

paras.en: “It is clear,” interrupted I-330, “that to be original means to stand out among others; consequently to be original means to violate the law of equality. What was called in the language of the ancients ‘to be common’ is with us only the fulfilling of one’s duty. For⁠—”
paras.uz: «Aniqki, — gapimni bo'ldi I-330, — o'ziga xos bo'lish boshqalardan ajralib turishni anglatadi; demak, o'ziga xos bo'lish tenglik qonunini buzishni anglatadi. Qadimgilar tilida "oddiy bo'lish" deb atalgan narsa bizda faqat o'z burchini bajarish. Chunki...»

paras.en: “Yes, yes, exactly,” I interrupted impatiently, “and there is no use, no use.⁠ ⁠…”
paras.uz: «Ha, ha, aynan shunday, — sabrsizlik bilan uning gapini bo'ldim, — va buning foydasi yo'q, foydasi yo'q...»

paras.en: She came near the bust of the snub-nosed poet, lowered the curtains on the wild fire of her eyes and said, this time I think she was really in earnest, or perhaps she merely wanted to soften my impatience with her, but she said a very reasonable thing:
paras.uz: U puchuq burunli shoirning byusti yoniga keldi, ko'zlarining yovvoyi olovi ustiga pardalarni tushirdi va dedi — menimcha, bu safar u haqiqatan ham jiddiy edi, yoki, ehtimol, shunchaki mening sabrsizligimni yumshatmoqchi bo'lgandir, lekin u juda oqilona gap aytdi:

paras.en: “Don’t you think it surprising that once people could stand types like this? Not only stand them but worship them. What a slavish spirit, don’t you think so?”
paras.uz: «Bir paytlar odamlar bunday tiplarga chiday olgani sizni hayratga solmaydimi? Nafaqat chidagan, balki ularga sig'inishgan. Qanday qullarcha ruh, shunday emasmi?»

paras.en: “It’s clear⁠ ⁠… that is⁠ ⁠… !” I wanted⁠ ⁠… (damn that cursed “it’s clear!”).
paras.uz: «Aniq... ya'ni...!» Men... istadim (la'nati «aniq»!).

paras.en: “Oh, yes, I understand. But in fact these were rulers stronger than the crowned ones. Why were they not isolated and exterminated? In our State⁠—”
paras.uz: «Oh, ha, tushunaman. Lekin aslida ular toj kiygan hukmdorlardan ham kuchliroq hukmdorlar edi. Nega ularni ajratib, yo'q qilishmagan? Bizning Davlatimizda...»

paras.en: “Oh, yes, in our State⁠—” I began.
paras.uz: «Oh, ha, bizning Davlatimizda...» — boshladim men.

paras.en: Suddenly she laughed. I saw the laughter in her eyes. I saw the resounding sharp curve of that laughter, flexible, tense like a whip. I remember my whole body shivered. I thought of grasping her⁠ ⁠… and I don’t know what.⁠ ⁠… I had to do something, mattered little what; automatically I looked at my golden badge, glanced at my watch⁠—ten minutes to seventeen!
paras.uz: To'satdan u kulib yubordi. Men kulgini uning ko'zlarida ko'rdim. Men o'sha kulgining jarangdor, o'tkir egri chizig'ini, qamchidek egiluvchan, taranglangan chizig'ini ko'rdim. Esimda, butun vujudim titrab ketdi. Uni ushlab olishni o'yladim... va nima qilishni bilmayman... Biror narsa qilishim kerak edi, nima bo'lishining farqi yo'q; mexanik ravishda oltin nishonimga qaradim, soatimga ko'z tashladim — o'n yettiga o'n daqiqa!

paras.en: “Don’t you think it is time to go?” I said in as polite a tone as possible.
paras.uz: «Ketish vaqti bo'ldi deb o'ylamaysizmi?» — dedim iloji boricha xushmuomala ohangda.

paras.en: “And if I should ask you to stay here with me?”
paras.uz: «Agar sizdan shu yerda men bilan qolishingizni so'rasam-chi?»

paras.en: “What? Do you realize what you are saying? In ten minutes I must be in the auditorium.”
paras.uz: «Nima? Nima deyayotganingizni tushunyapsizmi? O'n daqiqadan keyin men auditoriyada bo'lishim kerak».

paras.en: “And ‘all the Numbers must take the prescribed courses in art and science,’ ” said I-330 with my voice.
paras.uz: «Va "barcha Raqamlar san'at va fanlar bo'yicha belgilangan kurslardan o'tishlari shart"», — dedi I-330 mening ovozim bilan.

paras.en: Then she lifted the curtain, opened her eyes⁠—through the dark windows the fire was blazing.
paras.uz: Keyin u pardani ko'tardi, ko'zlarini ochdi — qorong'i derazalar orqali olov alangalanardi.

paras.en: “I have a physician in the Medical Bureau; he is registered to me; if I ask him, he will give you a certificate declaring that you are ill. All right?”
paras.uz: «Tibbiyot Byurosida mening bir shifokorim bor; u mening nomimga yozilgan; agar undan so'rasam, u sizga kasal ekaningiz haqida guvohnoma beradi. Xo'pmi?»

paras.en: Understood! At last I understood where this game was leading.
paras.uz: Tushundim! Nihoyat bu o'yin qayerga olib borayotganini tushundim.

paras.en: “Ah, so! But you know that every honest Number as a matter of course must immediately go to the office of the Guardians and⁠—”
paras.uz: «Ah, shunday! Lekin bilasizki, har bir halol Raqam o'z-o'zidan ravshan, darhol Qo'riqchilar idorasiga borishi va...»

paras.en: “And as a matter not of course?” (Sharp smile-bite) “I am very curious to know; will you or will you not go to the Guardians?”
paras.uz: «O'z-o'zidan ravshan bo'lmasa-chi?» (O'tkir tabassum-tishlash.) «Juda qiziqaman: siz Qo'riqchilarga borasizmi yoki yo'qmi?»

paras.en: “Are you going to remain here?”
paras.uz: «Siz shu yerda qolmoqchimisiz?»

paras.en: I grasped the knob of the door. It was a brass knob, a cold, brass knob and I heard, cold like brass, her voice:
paras.uz: Men eshik dastagini ushladim. U mis dastak edi, sovuq mis dastak va men misdek sovuq uning ovozini eshitdim:

paras.en: “Just a minute, may I?”
paras.uz: «Bir daqiqa, mumkinmi?»

paras.en: She went to the telephone, called a Number⁠—I was so upset it escaped me⁠—and spoke loudly: “I shall be waiting for you in the Ancient House. Yes, yes, alone.”
paras.uz: U telefonga bordi, bir Raqamni chaqirdi — men shunchalik hayajonda edimki, buni payqamay qoldim — va baland ovozda gapirdi: «Sizni Qadimiy Uyda kutaman. Ha, ha, yolg'iz».

paras.en: I turned the cold brass knob.
paras.uz: Men sovuq mis dastakni burdim.

paras.en: “May I take the aero?”
paras.uz: «Aeroni olsam bo'ladimi?»

paras.en: “Oh yes, certainly, please!”
paras.uz: «Oh, ha, albatta, marhamat!»

paras.en: In the sunshine at the gate the old woman was dozing like a plant. Again I was surprised to see her grown-together mouth open, and to hear her say:
paras.uz: Darvoza oldida, quyoshda kampir o'simlikdek mudrab o'tirardi. Yana uning bitib ketgan og'zi ochilganini ko'rib va uning gapirganini eshitib hayron bo'ldim:

paras.en: “And your lady, did she remain alone?”
paras.uz: «Xonimingiz-chi, u yolg'iz qoldimi?»

paras.en: “Alone.”
paras.uz: «Yolg'iz».

paras.en: The mouth of the old woman grew together again; she shook her head; apparently even her weakening brain understood the stupidity and the danger of the behaviour of that woman.
paras.uz: Kampirning og'zi yana bitib qoldi; u boshini chayqadi; aftidan, hatto uning zaiflashayotgan miyasi ham o'sha ayolning xatti-harakati qanchalik ahmoqona va xavfli ekanini tushundi.

paras.en: At seventeen o’clock exactly, I was at the lecture. There I suddenly realized that I did not tell the whole truth to the old woman. I-330 was not there alone now. Possibly this fact, that I involuntarily told the old woman a lie, was torturing me now and distracting my attention. Yes, not alone⁠—that was the point.
paras.uz: Aynan soat o'n yettida men ma'ruzada edim. U yerda to'satdan kampirga butun haqiqatni aytmaganimni angladim. I-330 hozir u yerda yolg'iz emasdi. Ehtimol, kampirga beixtiyor yolg'on gapirganim hozir meni qiynab, e'tiborimni chalg'itayotgandir. Ha, yolg'iz emas — gap shunda edi.

paras.en: After twenty-one-thirty o’clock I had a free hour. I could therefore have gone to the office of the Guardians to make my report; but after that stupid adventure I was so tired⁠—besides, the law provides two days. I shall have time tomorrow; I have another twenty-four hours.
paras.uz: Soat yigirma bir o'ttizdan keyin bo'sh soatim bor edi. Shuning uchun men xabar berish uchun Qo'riqchilar idorasiga borishim mumkin edi; lekin o'sha ahmoqona sarguzashtdan keyin men shunchalik charchagan edimki — bundan tashqari, qonun ikki kun muhlat beradi. Ertaga ulguraman; yana yigirma to'rt soatim bor.

gloss.ex: …330. I shall run over to you immediately. We shall go together to the Ancient House. Agreed?”
…d we found ourselves in a sombre disorderly space (they called it an “apartment”). The same strange “royal” musical instrument and a wild, unorganized, crazy lo…
“It’s clear that you want to seem original. But is it possible that you⁠—?”
…among others; consequently to be original means to violate the law of equality. What was called in the language of the ancients ‘to be common’ is with us only t…
…I could therefore have gone to the office of the Guardians to make my report; but after that stupid adventure I was so tired⁠—besides, the law provides two days…

quiz.why_uz: Ular Yashil Devor yonidagi Qadimiy Uyga borishadi.

o: A medical certificate saying he is ill
quiz.why_uz: U shifokor orqali kasallik haqida guvohnoma olib berishni taklif qiladi.

chapters.recap_uz: I-330 D-503 ni Qadimiy Uyga olib boradi, qadimiy libos kiyadi va uni ma'ruzaga bormay qolishga undaydi. D-503 Qo'riqchilarga xabar berishi kerak, lekin buni ertaga qoldiradi.

chapters.title: Record 7

paras.en: An eyelash⁠—Taylor⁠—Henbane and lily of the valley.
paras.uz: Kiprik — Teylor — Mingdevona va marvaridgul.

paras.en: Night. Green, orange, blue. The red royal instrument. The yellow dress. Then a brass Buddha. Suddenly it lifted the brass eyelids and sap began to flow from it, from Buddha. Sap also from the yellow dress. Even in the mirror⁠—drops of sap, and from the large bed and from the children’s bed and soon from myself.⁠ ⁠… It is horror, mortally sweet horror!⁠ ⁠…
paras.uz: Tun. Yashil, to'q sariq, moviy. Qizil qirollik cholg'usi. Sariq ko'ylak. Keyin mis Budda. To'satdan u mis qovoqlarini ko'tardi va undan, Buddadan shira oqa boshladi. Sariq ko'ylakdan ham shira. Hatto ko'zguda ham — shira tomchilari, katta karavotdan ham, bolalar karavotidan ham, tez orada o'zimdan ham... Bu dahshat, o'ldiradigan darajada shirin dahshat!..

paras.en: I woke up. Soft blue light, the glass of the walls, of the chairs, of the table was glimmering. This calmed me. My heart stopped palpitating. Sap! Buddha! How absurd! I am sick, it is clear; I never saw dreams before. They say that to see dreams was a common normal thing with the ancients. Yes, after all, their life was a whirling carousel: green, orange, Buddha, sap⁠—but we, people of today, we know all too well that dreaming is a serious mental disease. I.⁠ ⁠… Is it possible that my brain, this precise, clean, glittering mechanism, like a chronometer without a speck of dust on it, is⁠ ⁠… ? Yes it is, now. I really feel there in the brain some foreign body like an eyelash in the eye. One does not feel one’s whole body but this eye with a hair in it, one cannot forget it for a second.⁠ ⁠…
paras.uz: Uyg'onib ketdim. Yumshoq moviy yorug'lik, devorlarning, kursilarning, stolning shishasi yiltillardi. Bu meni tinchlantirdi. Yuragim qattiq urishdan to'xtadi. Shira! Budda! Qanday bema'nilik! Men kasalman, aniq; ilgari hech qachon tush ko'rmaganman. Aytishlaricha, qadimgilarda tush ko'rish oddiy, odatiy narsa bo'lgan. Ha, axir ularning hayoti aylanuvchi karusel edi: yashil, to'q sariq, Budda, shira — lekin biz, bugungi odamlar, tush ko'rish jiddiy ruhiy kasallik ekanini juda yaxshi bilamiz. Men... Nahotki mening miyam, bu aniq, toza, yaltiroq, ustida bir zarra chang bo'lmagan xronometrdek mexanizm... ? Ha, endi shunday. Men haqiqatan ham u yerda, miyada ko'zga tushgan kiprikdek qandaydir begona jismni his qilyapman. Butun tanangni his qilmaysan, lekin ichiga tuk tushgan bu ko'zni bir soniya ham unuta olmaysan...

paras.en: The cheerful, crystalline sound of the bell at my head. Seven o’clock. Time to get up. To the right and to the left as in mirrors, to the right and to the left through the glass walls I see others like myself, other rooms like my own, other clothes like my own, movements like mine, duplicated thousands of times. This invigorates me; I see myself as a part of an enormous, vigorous, united body; and what precise beauty! Not a single superfluous gesture, or bow, or turn. Yes, this Taylor was undoubtedly the greatest genius of the ancients. True, he did not come to the idea of applying his method to the whole life, to every step throughout the twenty-four hours of the day; he was unable to integrate his system from one o’clock to twenty-four. I cannot understand the ancients. How could they write whole libraries about some Kant and take notice only slightly of Taylor, of this prophet who saw ten centuries ahead?
paras.uz: Boshim ustidagi qo'ng'iroqning quvnoq, billur ovozi. Soat yetti. Turish vaqti. O'ngda va chapda, xuddi ko'zgulardagidek, o'ngda va chapda shisha devorlar orqali men o'zimga o'xshagan boshqalarni, o'z xonamga o'xshagan boshqa xonalarni, o'z kiyimimga o'xshagan boshqa kiyimlarni, minglab marta takrorlangan mening harakatlarimga o'xshagan harakatlarni ko'raman. Bu meni tetiklashtiradi; o'zimni ulkan, baquvvat, yagona tananing bir qismi sifatida ko'raman; va qanday aniq go'zallik! Birorta ham ortiqcha imo-ishora, egilish yoki burilish yo'q. Ha, bu Teylor, shubhasiz, qadimgilarning eng buyuk dahosi edi. To'g'ri, u o'z usulini butun hayotga, sutkaning yigirma to'rt soati davomidagi har bir qadamga qo'llash g'oyasiga kelmagan; u o'z tizimini soat birdan yigirma to'rtgacha integrallay olmagan. Qadimgilarni tushuna olmayman. Qanday qilib ular qandaydir Kant haqida butun kutubxonalar yozib, Teylorni — o'n asr oldinni ko'ra olgan bu payg'ambarni zo'rg'a payqashgan?

paras.en: Breakfast was over. The hymn of the United State had been harmoniously sung; rhythmically, four abreast we walked to the elevators, the motors buzzed faintly and swiftly we went down⁠—down⁠—down, the heart sinking slightly. Again that stupid dream or some unknown function of that dream. Oh, yes! Yesterday in the aero, then down⁠—down! Well, it is all over, anyhow. Period. It is very fortunate that I was so firm and brusque with her.
paras.uz: Nonushta tugadi. Yagona Davlat madhiyasi uyg'un kuylandi; ritmik ravishda, to'rttadan qator bo'lib liftlarga bordik, motorlar sekin g'uvilladi va biz tez pastga — pastga — pastga tushdik, yurak biroz tushib ketdi. Yana o'sha ahmoqona tush yoki o'sha tushning qandaydir noma'lum funksiyasi. Ha, to'g'ri! Kecha aeroda, keyin pastga — pastga! Xo'sh, har holda hammasi tugadi. Nuqta. U bilan shunchalik qat'iy va keskin bo'lganim juda yaxshi bo'ldi.

paras.en: The car of the underground railway carried me swiftly to the place where the motionless, beautiful body of the Integral, not yet spiritualized by fire, was glittering in the docks in the sunshine. With closed eyes I dreamed in formulae. Again I calculated in my mind what was the initial velocity required to tear away the Integral from the earth. Every second the mass of the Integral would change because of the expenditure of the explosive fuel. The equation was very complex with transcendant figures. As in a dream I felt, right here in the firm calculated world, how someone sat down at my side, barely touching me and saying, “Pardon.” I opened my eyes. At first, apparently because of an association with the Integral, I saw something impetuously flying into the distance: a head; I saw pink wing-ears sticking out on the sides of it, then the curve of the overhanging back of the head, the double-curved letter S.
paras.uz: Yer osti temir yo'lining vagoni meni tezda Integralning hali olov bilan jonlantirilmagan qimirlamas, go'zal tanasi stapelda quyoshda yaltirab turgan joyga olib keldi. Ko'zlarimni yumib, formulalar bilan tush ko'rdim. Yana xayolimda Integralni yerdan uzib olish uchun qanday boshlang'ich tezlik kerakligini hisobladim. Portlovchi yoqilg'i sarfi tufayli Integralning massasi har soniyada o'zgaradi. Tenglama transsendent kattaliklar bilan juda murakkab edi. Go'yo tushda, aynan shu mustahkam, hisoblangan dunyoda kimdir yonimga o'tirib, menga zo'rg'a tegib, «Kechirasiz» deganini his qildim. Ko'zlarimni ochdim. Avvaliga, aftidan, Integral bilan assotsiatsiya tufayli, uzoqqa shiddat bilan uchib ketayotgan nimanidir ko'rdim: bosh; uning yon tomonlaridan chiqib turgan pushti qanot-quloqlarni, keyin osilib turgan ensaning egri chizig'ini, ikki marta egilgan S harfini ko'rdim.

paras.en: Through the glass walls of my algebraic world, again I felt the eyelash in my eye. I felt something disagreeable, I felt that today I must.⁠ ⁠…
paras.uz: Algebraik dunyomning shisha devorlari orqali yana ko'zimdagi kiprikni his qildim. Nimadir yoqimsiz narsani his qildim, bugun men albatta...

paras.en: “Certainly, please,”⁠—I smiled at my neighbor and bowed.
paras.uz: «Albatta, marhamat», — men qo'shnimga jilmayib, ta'zim qildim.

paras.en: Number S-4711 I saw glittering on his golden badge (that is why I associated him with the letter S from the very first moment: an optical impression which remained unregistered by consciousness). His eyes sparkled, two sharp little drills; they were revolving swiftly, drilling in deeper and deeper. It seemed that in a moment they would drill in to the bottom and would see something that I do not even dare to confess to myself.⁠ ⁠…
paras.uz: Uning oltin nishonida yaltirayotgan S-4711 raqamini ko'rdim (shuning uchun ham birinchi lahzadanoq uni S harfi bilan bog'lagan edim: ong qayd etmagan optik taassurot). Uning ko'zlari ikki o'tkir parmadek chaqnardi; ular tez aylanib, tobora chuqurroq parmalab kirardi. Go'yo bir lahzadan keyin ular tubiga yetib, men o'zimga tan olishga ham jur'at etmaydigan nimanidir ko'radigandek tuyulardi...

paras.en: That bothersome eyelash became wholly clear to me. S- was one of them, one of the Guardians, and it would be the simplest thing immediately, without deferring to tell him everything!
paras.uz: O'sha jonga tegadigan kiprik menga butunlay ravshan bo'ldi. S- ulardan biri, Qo'riqchilardan biri edi va unga darhol, kechiktirmasdan hammasini aytish eng oddiy ish bo'lardi!

paras.en: “I went yesterday to the Ancient House⁠ ⁠…” my voice was strange, husky, flat⁠—I tried to cough.
paras.uz: «Kecha men Qadimiy Uyga bordim...» — ovozim g'alati, bo'g'iq, yassi chiqdi — yo'talib qo'yishga urindim.

paras.en: “That is good. It must have given you material for some instructive deductions.”
paras.uz: «Bu yaxshi. Bu sizga ibratli xulosalar uchun material bergan bo'lsa kerak».

paras.en: “Yes⁠ ⁠… but⁠ ⁠… You see, I was not alone; I was in the company of I-330, and then.⁠ ⁠…”
paras.uz: «Ha... lekin... Bilasizmi, men yolg'iz emasdim; men I-330 bilan birga edim, keyin esa...»

paras.en: “I-330? You are fortunate. She is a very interesting, gifted woman; she has a host of admirers.”
paras.uz: «I-330 bilanmi? Siz omadlisiz. U juda qiziqarli, iste'dodli ayol; uning muxlislari ko'p».

paras.en: But he too⁠—then during the promenade.⁠ ⁠… Perhaps he is even assigned as her he-Number! No, it is impossible to tell him, unthinkable. This was perfectly clear.
paras.uz: Lekin u ham — o'shanda sayr paytida... Ehtimol, u hatto uning erkak-Raqami sifatida yozilgandir! Yo'q, unga aytish mumkin emas, aqlga sig'maydi. Bu mutlaqo aniq edi.

paras.en: “Yes, yes, certainly, very,” I smiled, broader and broader, more stupidly, and felt as if my smile made me look foolish, naked.
paras.uz: «Ha, ha, albatta, juda», — men tobora kengroq, ahmoqonaroq jilmaydim va tabassumim meni ahmoq, yalang'och ko'rsatayotgandek his qildim.

paras.en: The drills reached the bottom; revolving continually they screwed themselves back into his eyes. S- smiled double-curvedly, nodded and slid to the exit.
paras.uz: Parmalar tubiga yetdi; to'xtovsiz aylanib, yana uning ko'zlariga burab kirib ketdi. S- ikki marta egilib jilmaydi, bosh irg'adi va chiqish tomon sirg'alib ketdi.

paras.en: I covered my face with the newspaper (I felt as if everybody were looking at me), and soon I forgot about the eyelash, about the little drills, about everything, I was so upset by what I read in the paper: “According to authentic information, traces of an organization which still remains out of reach, have again been discovered. This organization aims at liberation from the beneficial yoke of the State.”
paras.uz: Men yuzimni gazeta bilan to'sdim (go'yo hamma menga qarab turgandek tuyulardi) va tez orada kiprikni ham, parmachalarni ham, hamma narsani ham unutdim — gazetada o'qiganlarimdan shunchalik hayajonlandim: «Ishonchli ma'lumotlarga ko'ra, hali ham qo'lga tushmagan bir tashkilotning izlari yana topildi. Bu tashkilot Davlatning foydali bo'yinturug'idan ozod bo'lishni maqsad qilgan».

paras.en: Liberation! It is remarkable how persistent human criminal instincts are! I use deliberately the word “criminal,” for freedom and crime are as closely related as⁠—well, as the movement of an aero and its speed: if the speed of an aero equals zero, the aero is motionless; if human liberty is equal to zero, man does not commit any crime. That is clear. The way to rid man of criminality is to rid him of freedom. No sooner did we rid ourselves of freedom (in the cosmic sense centuries are only a “no sooner”), than suddenly some unknown pitiful degenerates.⁠ ⁠… No, I cannot understand why I did not go immediately yesterday to the Bureau of the Guardians. Today, after sixteen o’clock, I shall go there without fail.
paras.uz: Ozod bo'lish! Inson jinoiy instinktlari qanchalik qat'iyatli ekani ajablanarli! Men ataylab «jinoiy» so'zini ishlatyapman, chunki erkinlik va jinoyat bir-biri bilan xuddi... xo'sh, aeroning harakati va uning tezligi kabi chambarchas bog'liq: agar aeroning tezligi nolga teng bo'lsa, aero qimirlamaydi; agar inson erkinligi nolga teng bo'lsa, inson hech qanday jinoyat qilmaydi. Bu aniq. Insonni jinoyatchilikdan qutqarishning yo'li — uni erkinlikdan qutqarish. Biz erkinlikdan qutulishimiz bilanoq (kosmik ma'noda asrlar — faqat «bilanoq»), to'satdan qandaydir noma'lum ayanchli degeneratlar... Yo'q, kecha nega darhol Qo'riqchilar Idorasiga bormaganimni tushuna olmayman. Bugun soat o'n oltidan keyin albatta u yerga boraman.

paras.en: At sixteen-ten I was in the street; at once I noticed O-90 at the corner; she was all rosy with delight at the encounter. She has a simple, round mind. A timely meeting; she would understand and lend me support. Or,⁠ ⁠… no, I did not need any support; my decision was firm.
paras.uz: Soat o'n olti o'nda men ko'chada edim; burchakda darhol O-90 ni payqadim; u uchrashuvdan butunlay pushti tusga kirgan edi. Uning aqli oddiy, yumaloq. O'z vaqtidagi uchrashuv; u tushunadi va meni qo'llab-quvvatlaydi. Yoki... yo'q, menga hech qanday qo'llab-quvvatlash kerak emasdi; qarorim qat'iy edi.

paras.en: The pipes of the Musical Tower thundered out harmoniously the March⁠—the same daily March. How wonderful the charm of this dailiness, of this constant repetition and mirror-like smoothness!
paras.uz: Musiqa Minorasining quvurlari Marshni — o'sha kundalik Marshni uyg'un gumburlatardi. Bu kundaliklikning, bu doimiy takrorlanish va ko'zgudek silliqlikning jozibasi qanchalik ajoyib!

paras.en: “Out for a walk?” Her round blue eyes opened toward me widely, blue windows leading inside; I penetrate there unhindered; there is nothing in there, I mean nothing foreign, nothing superfluous.
paras.uz: «Sayrgami?» Uning yumaloq moviy ko'zlari menga keng ochildi, ichkariga olib boradigan moviy derazalar; men u yerga to'siqsiz kiraman; u yerda hech narsa yo'q, ya'ni begona hech narsa, ortiqcha hech narsa yo'q.

paras.en: “No, not for a walk. I must go.” I told her where. And to my astonishment I saw her rosy round mouth form a crescent with the horns downward as if she tasted something sour. This angered me.
paras.uz: «Yo'q, sayrga emas. Men borishim kerak». Qayerga ekanini aytdim. Va hayratimga uning pushti yumaloq og'zi go'yo nordon narsa tatib ko'rgandek uchlari pastga qaragan o'roqqa aylanganini ko'rdim. Bu meni g'azablantirdi.

paras.en: “You she-Numbers seem to be incurably eaten up by prejudices. You are absolutely unable to think abstractly. Forgive me the word but this I call bluntness of mind.”
paras.uz: «Sizlar, ayol-Raqamlar, xurofotlar tomonidan davolab bo'lmas darajada yeb qo'yilganga o'xshaysiz. Sizlar mavhum fikrlashga mutlaqo qodir emassiz. So'z uchun kechiring, lekin men buni aqlning o'tmasligi deyman».

paras.en: “You?⁠ ⁠… to the spies? How ugly! And I went to the Botanical Garden and brought you a branch of lily-of-the-valley.⁠ ⁠…”
paras.uz: «Siz?.. josuslarning oldigami? Qanday xunuk! Men esa Botanika bog'iga borib, sizga marvaridgul shoxchasini olib keldim...»

paras.en: “Why, ‘and I’? Why this ‘and’? Just like a woman!”
paras.uz: «Nega "men esa"? Nega bu "esa"? Xuddi ayollardek!»

paras.en: Angrily (this I must confess), I snatched the flowers. “Here they are, your lilies-of-the-valley. Well, smell them! Good? Yes? Why not use a little bit of logic? The lilies-of-the-valley smell good; all right! But you cannot say about an odor, about the conception of an odor, that it is good or bad, can you? You can’t, can you? There is the smell of lilies-of-the-valley and there is the disagreeable smell of henbane. Both are odors. The ancient States had their spies; we have ours⁠ ⁠… yes, spies! I am not afraid of words. But is it not clear to you that there the spies were henbane; here they are lilies-of-the-valley? Yes, lilies-of-the-valley, yes!”
paras.uz: G'azab bilan (buni tan olishim kerak) gullarni tortib oldim. «Mana ular, marvaridgullaringiz. Qani, hidlang! Yaxshimi? Ha? Nega ozgina mantiq ishlatmaysiz? Marvaridgullar yaxshi hid taratadi; mayli! Lekin hid haqida, hid tushunchasi haqida uni yaxshi yoki yomon deb ayta olmaysiz-ku? Ayta olmaysiz, shundaymi? Marvaridgulning hidi bor, mingdevonaning yoqimsiz hidi bor. Ikkalasi ham hid. Qadimiy davlatlarning o'z josuslari bo'lgan; bizning ham o'zimiznikilar bor... ha, josuslar! Men so'zlardan qo'rqmayman. Lekin u yerda josuslar mingdevona, bu yerda esa marvaridgul ekani sizga aniq emasmi? Ha, marvaridgul, ha!»

paras.en: The rosy crescent quivered. Now I understand that it was only my impression but at that moment I was certain she was going to laugh. I shouted still louder:
paras.uz: Pushti o'roq titradi. Endi tushunamanki, bu faqat menga shunday tuyulgan, lekin o'sha lahzada u kulib yuboradi deb ishonchim komil edi. Men yanada balandroq qichqirdim:

paras.en: “Yes, lilies-of-the-valley! And there is nothing funny about it, nothing funny!”
paras.uz: «Ha, marvaridgul! Bunda kulgili hech narsa yo'q, kulgili hech narsa!»

paras.en: The smooth round globes of heads passing by were turning towards us. O-90 gently took my hand.
paras.uz: Yonimizdan o'tayotgan silliq yumaloq boshlar bizga qarab o'girilardi. O-90 qo'limni muloyimlik bilan ushladi.

paras.en: “You are so strange today⁠ ⁠… are you ill?”
paras.uz: «Bugun siz shunchalik g'alatisiz... kasal emasmisiz?»

paras.en: My dream.⁠ ⁠… Yellow color.⁠ ⁠… Buddha.⁠ ⁠… It was at once born clearly upon me that I must go to the Medical Bureau.
paras.uz: Tushim... Sariq rang... Budda... Darhol Tibbiyot Byurosiga borishim kerakligi menga aniq ayon bo'ldi.

paras.en: “Yes, you are right, I am sick,” I said with joy (that seems to me an inexplicable contradiction; there was nothing to be joyful about).
paras.uz: «Ha, siz haqsiz, men kasalman», — dedim quvonch bilan (bu menga tushuntirib bo'lmas ziddiyatdek tuyuladi; quvonish uchun hech narsa yo'q edi).

paras.en: “You must go at once to the doctor. You understand that; you are obliged to be healthy; it seems strange to have to prove it to you.”
paras.uz: «Siz darhol shifokorga borishingiz kerak. Tushunasiz-ku; siz sog'lom bo'lishga majbursiz; buni sizga isbotlashga to'g'ri kelishi g'alati».

paras.en: “My dear O-, of course you are right. Absolutely right.”
paras.uz: «Aziz O-, albatta, siz haqsiz. Mutlaqo haqsiz».

paras.en: I did not go to the Bureau of the Guardians; I could not; I had to go to the Medical Bureau; they kept me there until seventeen o’clock.
paras.uz: Men Qo'riqchilar Idorasiga bormadim; bora olmadim; Tibbiyot Byurosiga borishim kerak edi; u yerda meni soat o'n yettigacha ushlab turishdi.

paras.en: In the evening (incidentally, the Bureau of Guardians is closed evenings)⁠—in the evening O- came to see me. The curtains were not lowered. We busied ourselves with the arithmetical problems of an ancient textbook. This occupation always calms and purifies our thoughts. O- sat over her note book, her head slightly inclined to the left; she was so assiduous that she poked out her left cheek with the tongue from within. She looked so childlike, so charming.⁠ ⁠… I felt everything in me was pleasant, precise and simple.
paras.uz: Kechqurun (aytgancha, Qo'riqchilar Idorasi kechqurunlari yopiq) — kechqurun O- meni ko'rgani keldi. Pardalar tushirilmadi. Biz qadimiy darslikdagi arifmetik masalalar bilan shug'ullandik. Bu mashg'ulot doim fikrlarimizni tinchlantiradi va poklaydi. O- boshini biroz chapga egib, daftari ustida o'tirardi; u shunchalik tirishqoq ediki, chap yonog'ini ichkaridan tili bilan bo'rttirib qo'ygan edi. U shunchalik bolalarcha, shunchalik maftunkor ko'rinardi... Ichimdagi hamma narsa yoqimli, aniq va oddiy ekanini his qildim.

paras.en: She left. I remained alone. I breathed deeply two times (it is very good exercise before retiring for the night). Suddenly⁠—an unexpected odor reminiscent of something very disagreeable! I soon found out what was the matter: a branch of lily-of-the-valley was hidden in my bed. Immediately everything was aroused again, came up from the bottom. Decidedly, it was tactless on her part surreptitiously to put these lilies-of-the-valley there. Well, true I did not go; I didn’t, but was it my fault that I felt indisposed?
paras.uz: U ketdi. Men yolg'iz qoldim. Ikki marta chuqur nafas oldim (bu yotishdan oldin juda yaxshi mashq). To'satdan — juda yoqimsiz narsani eslatuvchi kutilmagan hid! Tez orada gap nimadaligini bildim: to'shagimga marvaridgul shoxchasi yashirib qo'yilgan edi. Darhol hamma narsa yana qo'zg'aldi, tubidan ko'tarildi. Albatta, bu marvaridgullarni u yerga yashirincha qo'yishi uning tomonidan nazokatsizlik edi. Xo'sh, to'g'ri, men bormadim; bormadim, lekin tobim yo'qligi mening aybimmi?

gloss.ex: …t is, now. I really feel there in the brain some foreign body like an eyelash in the eye. One does not feel one’s whole body but this eye with a hair in it, one…
…itating. Sap! Buddha! How absurd! I am sick, it is clear; I never saw dreams before. They say that to see dreams was a common normal thing with the ancients. Ye…
…smell of lilies-of-the-valley and there is the disagreeable smell of henbane. Both are odors. The ancient States had their spies; we have ours⁠ ⁠… yes, spies!…

quiz.q: What does D-503 think dreaming is?
quiz.why_uz: Uning fikricha, tush ko'rish jiddiy ruhiy kasallik.
S-4711 — Qo'riqchilardan biri.

chapters.recap_uz: D-503 birinchi marta tush ko'radi va o'zini kasal deb biladi. Poyezdda S-4711 bilan uchrashadi, keyin O-90 olib kelgan marvaridgullar ustida josuslar haqida bahslashadi va Qo'riqchilar o'rniga Tibbiyot Byurosiga boradi.

chapters.title: Record 8

paras.en: An irrational root⁠—R-13⁠—The triangle.
paras.uz: Irratsional ildiz — R-13 — Uchburchak.

paras.en: It was long ago during my schooldays, when I first encountered the square-root of minus one. I remember it all very clearly; a bright globe-like class hall, about a hundred round heads of children and Plappa⁠—our mathematician. We nicknamed him Plappa; it was a very much used-up mathematician, loosely screwed together; as the member of the class who was on duty that day would be putting the plug into the socket behind we would hear at first from the megaphone, “Plap-plap-plap-plap⁠—tshshsh.⁠ ⁠…” Only then the lesson would follow. One day Plappa told us about irrational numbers, and I remember I wept and banged the table with my fist and cried, “I do not want that square-root of minus one; take that square-root of minus one away!” This irrational root grew into me as something strange, foreign, terrible; it tortured me; it could not be thought out. It could not be defeated because it was beyond reason.
paras.uz: Bu ancha oldin, maktab yillarimda, minus birdan kvadrat ildizga birinchi marta duch kelganimda bo'lgan. Hammasini juda aniq eslayman: yorug' shardek sinf xonasi, yuzga yaqin bolalarning yumaloq boshlari va Plyappa — matematigimiz. Biz uni Plyappa deb laqab qo'ygan edik; u juda eskirgan, bo'sh burab yig'ilgan matematik edi; o'sha kuni navbatchi bo'lgan sinf a'zosi orqadagi rozetkaga vilkani suqayotganda, karnaydan avval «Plyap-plyap-plyap-plyap — tsh-sh-sh...» degan ovoz eshitilardi. Faqat shundan keyin dars boshlanardi. Bir kuni Plyappa bizga irratsional sonlar haqida gapirib berdi va esimda, men yig'lab, stolni mushtim bilan urib qichqirdim: «Men bu minus birdan kvadrat ildizni istamayman; bu minus birdan kvadrat ildizni olib tashlang!» Bu irratsional ildiz ichimga g'alati, begona, dahshatli narsa bo'lib o'sib kirdi; u meni qiynardi; uni o'ylab yechib bo'lmasdi. Uni yengib bo'lmasdi, chunki u aqldan tashqarida edi.

paras.en: Now that square-root of minus one is here again. I read over what I have written and I clearly see that I was insincere with myself, that I lied to myself in order to avoid seeing that square-root of minus one. My sickness, etc., is all nonsense; I could go there. I feel sure that if such a thing had happened a week ago I should have gone without hesitating. Why then am I unable to go now?⁠ ⁠… Why?
paras.uz: Endi o'sha minus birdan kvadrat ildiz yana shu yerda. Yozganlarimni qayta o'qidim va o'zimga nisbatan samimiy bo'lmaganimni, o'sha minus birdan kvadrat ildizni ko'rmaslik uchun o'zimga yolg'on gapirganimni aniq ko'ryapman. Kasalligim va hokazo — hammasi bema'nilik; u yerga bora olardim. Ishonchim komilki, agar bunday narsa bir hafta oldin sodir bo'lganida, ikkilanmasdan borgan bo'lardim. Unda nega hozir bora olmayapman?.. Nega?

paras.en: Today, for instance, at exactly sixteen-ten I stood before the glittering Glass Wall. Above was the shining, golden, sun-like sign: “Bureau of Guardians.” Inside, a long queue of bluish-gray unifs awaiting their turns, faces shining like the oil lamps in an ancient temple. They came to accomplish a great thing: they came to put on the altar of the United State their beloved ones, their friends, their own selves. My whole being craved to join them, yet⁠ ⁠… I could not; my feet were as though melted into the glass plates of the sidewalk. I simply stood there looking foolish.
paras.uz: Masalan, bugun aynan soat o'n olti o'nda men yaltirayotgan Shisha Devor oldida turdim. Tepada yaltiroq, oltin, quyoshdek yozuv: «Qo'riqchilar Idorasi». Ichkarida navbatini kutayotgan kulrang-moviy yunifalarning uzun navbati, yuzlari qadimiy ibodatxonadagi moy chiroqlardek porlardi. Ular buyuk ishni bajarish uchun kelishgan: ular Yagona Davlat qurbongohiga sevganlarini, do'stlarini, o'zlarini qo'yish uchun kelishgan. Butun vujudim ularga qo'shilishni istardi, lekin... bora olmadim; oyoqlarim yo'lkaning shisha plitalariga erib yopishib qolgandek edi. Men shunchaki ahmoqona turib qoldim.

paras.en: “Heh, mathematician! Dreaming?”
paras.uz: «He, matematik! Xayol suryapsanmi?»

paras.en: I shivered. Black eyes varnished with laughter looked at me⁠—thick negro lips! It was my old friend the poet, R-13, and with him rosy O-. I turned around angrily (I still believe that if they had not appeared I should have entered the Bureau and have torn the square-root of minus one out of my flesh).
paras.uz: Seskanib ketdim. Kulgi bilan laklangan qora ko'zlar menga qarab turardi — qalin negr lablari! Bu eski do'stim shoir R-13 edi, u bilan birga pushti O-. Men g'azab bilan o'girildim (hali ham ishonamanki, agar ular paydo bo'lmaganida, men Idoraga kirib, minus birdan kvadrat ildizni etimdan yulib tashlagan bo'lardim).

paras.en: “Not dreaming at all; if you will, ‘standing in adoration,’ ” I retorted quite brusquely.
paras.uz: «Umuman xayol surayotganim yo'q; xohlasang, "hayrat bilan sajda qilib turibman"», — ancha keskin javob qaytardim.

paras.en: “Oh, certainly, certainly! You, my friend, should never have become a mathematician; you should have become a poet, a great poet! Yes, come over to our trade, to the poets. Heh? If you will, I can arrange it in a jiffy. Heh?”
paras.uz: «Oh, albatta, albatta! Sen, do'stim, hech qachon matematik bo'lmasliging kerak edi; sen shoir, buyuk shoir bo'lishing kerak edi! Ha, bizning hunarimizga, shoirlarga o't. He? Xohlasang, buni bir zumda tashkil qila olaman. He?»

paras.en: R-13 usually talks very fast: His words run in torrents, his thick lips sprinkle. Every p is a fountain, every “poets” a fountain.
paras.uz: R-13 odatda juda tez gapiradi: uning so'zlari sel bo'lib oqadi, qalin lablaridan sachraydi. Har bir «p» — favvora, har bir «poetlar» — favvora.

paras.en: “So far I have served knowledge, and I shall continue to serve knowledge.”
paras.uz: «Shu paytgacha men bilimga xizmat qilganman va bilimga xizmat qilishda davom etaman».

paras.en: I frowned. I do not like, I do not understand jokes, and R-13 has the bad habit of joking.
paras.uz: Men qovog'imni soldim. Men hazillarni yoqtirmayman, tushunmayman, R-13 ning esa hazillashadigan yomon odati bor.

paras.en: “Heh, to the deuce with knowledge. Your much-heralded knowledge is but a form of cowardice. It is a fact! Yes, you want to encircle the infinite with a wall and you fear to cast a glance behind the wall. Yes, sir! And if ever you should glance beyond the wall you would be dazzled and close your eyes⁠—yes⁠—”
paras.uz: «He, bilimni jin ursin! Sen ko'p maqtaydigan bilim — qo'rqoqlikning bir shakli, xolos. Bu haqiqat! Ha, sen cheksizlikni devor bilan o'rab olmoqchisan va devor ortiga qarashdan qo'rqasan. Ha, janob! Agar qachondir devor ortiga qarasang, ko'zing qamashib, ko'zlaringni yumib olasan — ha...»

paras.en: “Walls are the foundation of every human⁠—” I began.
paras.uz: «Devorlar har qanday insoniy narsaning poydevori...» — boshladim men.

paras.en: R-13 sprinkled his fountain. O- laughed rosily and roundly. I waved my hand: “Well, you may laugh, I don’t care.” I was busy with something else. I had to find a way of eating up, of crushing down, that square-root of minus one. “Suppose,” I offered, “we go to my place and do some arithmetical problems.” (The quiet hour of yesterday afternoon came to my memory; perhaps today also.⁠ ⁠…)
paras.uz: R-13 favvorasini sachratdi. O- pushti va yumaloq kuldi. Men qo'l siltadim: «Xo'sh, kulaveringlar, menga baribir». Men boshqa narsa bilan band edim. O'sha minus birdan kvadrat ildizni yeb yuborish, ezib tashlash yo'lini topishim kerak edi. «Keling, — taklif qildim men, — menikiga borib, arifmetik masalalar yechamiz». (Kechagi tushdan keyingi sokin soat yodimga tushdi; ehtimol, bugun ham...)

paras.en: O- glanced at R-, then serenely and roundly at me; the soft, endearing color of our pink checks came to her cheeks.
paras.uz: O- R- ga qaradi, keyin xotirjam va yumaloq menga qaradi; yonoqlariga pushti chiptalarimizning yumshoq, mehrli rangi chiqdi.

paras.en: “But today I am.⁠ ⁠… I have a check to him today.” (A glance at R-.) “And tonight he is busy, so that⁠—”
paras.uz: «Lekin bugun men... Bugun menda unga chipta bor». (R- ga qarash.) «Kechqurun esa u band, shuning uchun...»

paras.en: The moist varnished lips whispered good-naturedly: “Half an hour is plenty for us, is it not, O-? I am not a great lover of your problems; let us simply go over to my place and chat.”
paras.uz: Ho'l, laklangan lablar xushfe'llik bilan pichirladi: «Bizga yarim soat yetadi, shunday emasmi, O-? Men sening masalalaringning unchalik ishqibozi emasman; keling, shunchaki menikiga borib, gaplashamiz».

paras.en: I was afraid to remain alone with myself, or to be more correct, with that new strange self, who by some curious coincidence bore my number, D-503. So I went with R-. True, he is not precise, not rhythmic, his logic is jocular and turned inside out, yet we are.⁠ ⁠… Three years ago we both chose our dear, rosy O-. This tied our friendship more firmly together than our schooldays did. In R-’s room everything seems like mine; the Tables, the glass of the chairs, the table, the closet, the bed. But as we entered, R- moved one chair out of place, then another⁠—the room became confused, everything lost the established order and seemed to violate every rule of Euclid’s geometry. R- remained the same as before; in Taylor and in mathematics he always lagged at the tail of the class.
paras.uz: Men o'zim bilan, aniqrog'i, qandaydir g'alati tasodif bilan mening raqamimni — D-503 ni ko'tarib yurgan o'sha yangi g'alati o'zim bilan yolg'iz qolishdan qo'rqardim. Shuning uchun R- bilan bordim. To'g'ri, u aniq emas, ritmik emas, uning mantig'i hazilkash va teskari ag'darilgan, lekin biz... Uch yil oldin ikkalamiz aziz, pushti O- ni tanlagan edik. Bu do'stligimizni maktab yillarimizdan ham mustahkamroq bog'ladi. R- ning xonasida hamma narsa meniki kabi ko'rinadi; Jadval, kursilarning shishasi, stol, shkaf, karavot. Lekin biz kirganimizda R- bitta kursini joyidan surdi, keyin boshqasini — xona chalkashib ketdi, hamma narsa o'rnatilgan tartibini yo'qotdi va Evklid geometriyasining har bir qoidasini buzayotgandek ko'rindi. R- avvalgidek qoldi; Teylor va matematikada u doim sinfning dumida qolardi.

paras.en: We recalled Plappa, how we boys used to paste the whole surface of his glass legs with paper notes expressing our thanks (we all loved Plappa). We recalled our priest (it goes without saying that we were taught not the “law” of ancient religion but the law of the United State). Our priest had a very powerful voice; a real hurricane would come out of the megaphone. And we children would yell the prescribed texts after him with all our lung-power. We recalled how our scapegrace, R-13, used to stuff the priest with chewed paper; every word was thus accompanied by a paper wad shot out. Naturally, R- was punished, for what he did was undoubtedly wrong, but now we laughed heartily;⁠—by we I mean our triangle, R-, O-, and I, I must confess, I too.
paras.uz: Plyappani esladik, biz bolalar uning shisha oyoqlarining butun yuzasini minnatdorchilik bildiruvchi qog'oz yozuvlar bilan qanday yopishtirib chiqqanimizni (biz hammamiz Plyappani yaxshi ko'rardik). Ruhoniymizni esladik (o'z-o'zidan ravshanki, bizga qadimiy dinning «qonuni» emas, Yagona Davlat qonuni o'rgatilardi). Ruhoniymizning juda kuchli ovozi bor edi; karnaydan haqiqiy bo'ron chiqardi. Biz bolalar esa belgilangan matnlarni uning ortidan butun o'pkamiz bilan baqirib takrorlardik. Bizning sho'x bolamiz R-13 ruhoniyni chaynalgan qog'oz bilan qanday to'ldirib tashlaganini esladik; har bir so'zga shu tarzda otilgan qog'oz to'pi hamroh bo'lardi. Tabiiyki, R- jazolangan, chunki uning qilgan ishi, shubhasiz, noto'g'ri edi, lekin hozir biz chin dildan kuldik; — «biz» deganda uchburchagimizni — R-, O- va meni nazarda tutyapman, tan olishim kerak, men ham.

paras.en: “And what if he had been a living one? Like the ancient ones, heh?” We’d have b⁠ ⁠… b⁠ ⁠… , a fountain running from the fat bubbling lips. The sun was shining through the ceiling, the sun above, the sun from the sides, its reflection from below. O- on R-13’s lap and minute drops of sunlight in O-’s blue eyes. Somehow my heart warmed up. The square-root of minus one became silent and motionless.⁠ ⁠…
paras.uz: «Agar u tirik bo'lganida-chi? Qadimgilardagidek, a?» Biz u... u... — semiz, ko'pikli lablardan favvora oqardi. Quyosh shift orqali porlardi, tepada quyosh, yonlardan quyosh, pastdan uning aksi. O- R-13 ning tizzasida va O- ning moviy ko'zlarida mitti quyosh tomchilari. Negadir yuragim iliqlashdi. Minus birdan kvadrat ildiz jim va qimirlamay qoldi...

paras.en: “Well, how is your Integral? Will you soon hop off to enlighten the inhabitants of the planets? You’d better hurry up, my boy, or we poets will have produced such a devilish lot that even your Integral will be unable to lift the cargo. ‘Every day from eight to eleven’⁠ ⁠…” R- wagged his head and scratched the back of it. The back of his head is square; it looks like a little valise (I recalled for some reason an ancient painting In the Cab). I felt more lively.
paras.uz: «Xo'sh, Integraling qalay? Tez orada sayyoralar aholisini ma'rifatli qilish uchun uchib ketasanmi? Shoshilganing ma'qul, bolam, aks holda biz shoirlar shunchalik ko'p narsa yozib tashlaymizki, hatto Integraling ham yukni ko'tara olmaydi. "Har kuni soat sakkizdan o'n birgacha"...» R- boshini silkitib, ensasini qashidi. Uning ensasi kvadrat; u kichkina chamadonga o'xshaydi (negadir qadimiy «Izvoshda» degan surat yodimga tushdi). O'zimni jonlanganroq his qildim.

paras.en: “You too are writing for the Integral? Tell me about it. What are you writing about? What did you write today, for instance?”
paras.uz: «Sen ham Integral uchun yozyapsanmi? Gapirib ber. Nima haqida yozyapsan? Masalan, bugun nima yozding?»

paras.en: “Today I did not write; today I was busy with something else.” “B-b-busy” sprinkled straight into my face.
paras.uz: «Bugun yozmadim; bugun boshqa narsa bilan band edim». «B-b-band» to'g'ri yuzimga sachradi.

paras.en: “What else?”
paras.uz: «Nima bilan?»

paras.en: R- frowned. “What? What? Well, if you insist I’ll tell you. I was busy with the Death Sentence. I was putting the Death Sentence into verse. An idiot⁠—and to be frank, one of our poets.⁠ ⁠… For two years we all lived side by side with him and nothing seemed wrong. Suddenly he went crazy. ‘I,’ said he, ‘am a genius! And I am above the law.’ All that sort of nonsense.⁠ ⁠… But it is not a thing to talk about.”
paras.uz: R- qovog'ini soldi. «Nima? Nima? Xo'sh, qistasang, aytaman. Men O'lim hukmi bilan band edim. O'lim hukmini she'rga solayotgan edim. Bir telba — ochig'ini aytsam, shoirlarimizdan biri... Ikki yil davomida hammamiz u bilan yonma-yon yashadik va hech narsa noto'g'ri ko'rinmadi. To'satdan u aqldan ozdi. "Men, — dedi u, — dahoman! Men qonundan ustunman". Shunga o'xshash bema'ni gaplar... Lekin bu gaplashadigan narsa emas».

paras.en: The fat lips hung down. The varnish disappeared from the eyes. He jumped up, turned around and stared through the wall. I looked at his tightly closed little “valise” and thought, “What is he handling in his little valise now?”
paras.uz: Semiz lablar osilib tushdi. Ko'zlaridan lak g'oyib bo'ldi. U sakrab turdi, o'girildi va devor orqali tikilib qoldi. Men uning mahkam yopiq kichkina «chamadon»iga qarab o'yladim: «U hozir o'z chamadonchasida nimani titkilayotgan ekan?»

paras.en: A moment of awkward asymmetric silence. I could not see clearly what was the matter but I was certain there was something.⁠ ⁠…
paras.uz: Bir lahzalik noqulay, nosimmetrik sukut. Men gap nimadaligini aniq ko'ra olmadim, lekin nimadir borligiga ishonchim komil edi...

paras.en: “Fortunately the antediluvian time of those Shakespeares and Dostoevskys (or what were their names?) is past,” I said in a voice deliberately loud.
paras.uz: «Baxtimizga, o'sha Shekspirlar va Dostoyevskiylarning (yoki ularning ismi nima edi?) to'fondan oldingi zamoni o'tib ketdi», — dedim men ataylab baland ovozda.

paras.en: R- turned his face to me. Words sprinkled and bubbled out of him as before, but I thought I noticed there was no more joyful varnish to his eyes.
paras.uz: R- yuzini menga o'girdi. So'zlar undan avvalgidek sachrab, ko'piklanib chiqardi, lekin menga uning ko'zlarida endi quvonchli lak yo'qdek tuyuldi.

paras.en: “Yes, dear mathematician, fortunately, fortunately. We are the happy arithmetical mean. As you would put it, the integration from zero to infinity, from imbeciles to Shakespeare. Do I put it right?”
paras.uz: «Ha, aziz matematik, baxtimizga, baxtimizga. Biz baxtli o'rta arifmetikmiz. Sen aytgandek, noldan cheksizlikkacha, ahmoqlardan Shekspirgacha integrallash. To'g'ri aytyapmanmi?»

paras.en: I do not know why (it seemed to me absolutely uncalled for) I recalled suddenly the other one, her tone. A thin invisible thread stretched between her and R- (what thread?). The square-root of minus one began to bother me again. I glanced at my badge; sixteen-twenty-five o’clock! They had only thirty-five minutes for the use of the pink check.
paras.uz: Nima uchunligini bilmayman (bu menga mutlaqo o'rinsiz tuyuldi), to'satdan o'sha boshqasini, uning ohangini esladim. U bilan R- o'rtasida ingichka ko'rinmas ip tortilgan edi (qanday ip?). Minus birdan kvadrat ildiz yana meni bezovta qila boshladi. Nishonimga qaradim; soat o'n olti yigirma besh! Ularning pushti chiptadan foydalanish uchun atigi o'ttiz besh daqiqasi qolgan edi.

paras.en: “Well, I must go.” I kissed O-, shook hands with R- and went to the elevator.
paras.uz: «Xo'sh, men borishim kerak». O- ni o'pdim, R- bilan qo'l berib ko'rishdim va liftga yo'l oldim.

paras.en: As I crossed the avenue I turned around. Here and there in the huge mass of glass penetrated by sunshine there were grayish-blue squares, the opaque squares of lowered curtains⁠—the squares of rhythmic, Taylorized happiness. On the seventh floor I found R-13’s square. The curtains were already lowered.
paras.uz: Xiyobonni kesib o'tayotib ortimga o'girildim. Quyosh teshib o'tgan ulkan shisha massada u yer-bu yerda kulrang-moviy kvadratlar, tushirilgan pardalarning shaffof bo'lmagan kvadratlari bor edi — ritmik, teylorlashtirilgan baxtning kvadratlari. Yettinchi qavatda R-13 ning kvadratini topdim. Pardalar allaqachon tushirilgan edi.

paras.en: Dear O-.⁠ ⁠… Dear R-.⁠ ⁠… He also has (I do not know why I write this “also,” but I write as it comes from my pen), he too has something which is not entirely clear in him. Yet I, he and O-, we are a triangle; I confess, not an isosceles triangle but a triangle nevertheless. We, to speak in the language of our ancestors (perhaps to you, my planetary readers, this is the more comprehensible language) we are a family. And one feels so good at times, when one is able for a short while, at least, to close oneself within a firm triangle, to close oneself away from anything that.⁠ ⁠…
paras.uz: Aziz O-... Aziz R-... Unda ham (nega bu «ham»ni yozayotganimni bilmayman, lekin qalamimdan qanday chiqsa, shunday yozaman), unda ham to'liq tushunarli bo'lmagan nimadir bor. Shunga qaramay, men, u va O- — biz uchburchakmiz; tan olaman, teng yonli uchburchak emas, lekin baribir uchburchak. Biz, ajdodlarimiz tilida gapirsak (ehtimol, sizga, sayyoradagi o'quvchilarim, bu tushunarliroq tildir), biz — oilamiz. Va hech bo'lmaganda qisqa vaqtga mustahkam uchburchak ichiga yopilib, o'zingni har qanday narsadan, ...dan yopib olish ba'zan shunchalik yoqimli...

gloss.ex: “So far I have served knowledge, and I shall continue to serve knowledge.”
…e deuce with knowledge. Your much-heralded knowledge is but a form of cowardice. It is a fact! Yes, you want to encircle the infinite with a wall and you fear t…
…was undoubtedly wrong, but now we laughed heartily;⁠—by we I mean our triangle, R-, O-, and I, I must confess, I too.
…he back of it. The back of his head is square; it looks like a little valise (I recalled for some reason an ancient painting In the Cab). I felt more lively.

o: The square root of minus one
quiz.why_uz: √-1 uning uchun aqlga sig'maydigan, yengib bo'lmas narsa edi.
D-503, O-90 va R-13 — «oila» uchburchagi.

chapters.recap_uz: D-503 Qo'riqchilar Idorasi oldida turib, ichkariga kira olmaydi. R-13 va O-90 bilan uchrashib, R-13 xonasida o'tmishni eslaydi; ularning uchburchagi haqida o'ylaydi.

chapters.title: Record 9

paras.en: Liturgy⁠—Iambus⁠—The cast-iron hand.
paras.uz: Liturgiya — Yamb — Cho'yan qo'l.

paras.en: A solemn bright day. On such days one forgets one’s weaknesses, inexactitudes, illnesses, and everything is crystalline and imperturbable like our new glass.⁠ ⁠…
paras.uz: Tantanali, yorug' kun. Bunday kunlarda odam o'z zaifliklari, noaniqliklari, kasalliklarini unutadi va hamma narsa bizning yangi shishamiz kabi billurdek va sarsilmasdir...

paras.en: The Plaza of the Cube. Sixty-six imposing concentric circles⁠—stands. Sixty-six rows of quiet serene faces. Eyes reflecting the shining of the sky⁠—or perhaps it is the shining of the United State. Red like blood, are the flowers⁠—the lips of the women. Like soft garlands the faces of the children in the first rows, nearest the place of action. Profound, austere, gothic silence.
paras.uz: Kub maydoni. Oltmish olti ta salobatli konsentrik doira — tribunalar. Oltmish olti qator sokin, osoyishta yuzlar. Osmon nurini aks ettirgan ko'zlar — yoki, ehtimol, bu Yagona Davlatning nuridir. Qondek qizil gullar — ayollarning lablari. Harakat joyiga eng yaqin birinchi qatorlarda yumshoq gulchambarlardek bolalarning yuzlari. Chuqur, qattiq, gotik sukunat.

paras.en: To judge by the descriptions which reach us from the ancients, they felt somewhat like this during their “Church services,” but they served their nonsensical unknown god; we serve our rational god, whom we most thoroughly know. Their god gave them nothing but eternal, torturing seeking; our god gives us absolute truth, that is, he has rid us of any kind of doubt. Their god did not invent anything cleverer than sacrificing oneself, nobody knows what for; we bring to our god, The United State, a quiet, rational, carefully thought-out sacrifice.
paras.uz: Qadimgilardan bizga yetib kelgan tasvirlarga qaraganda, ular o'zlarining «ibodatlari» paytida shunga o'xshash narsani his qilishgan, lekin ular o'zlarining bema'ni, noma'lum xudolariga xizmat qilishgan; biz esa juda yaxshi biladigan oqilona xudoyimizga xizmat qilamiz. Ularning xudosi ularga abadiy, qiynovchi izlanishdan boshqa hech narsa bermagan; bizning xudoyimiz bizga mutlaq haqiqatni beradi, ya'ni bizni har qanday shubhadan xalos qilgan. Ularning xudosi kim biladi nima uchun o'zini qurbon qilishdan aqlliroq narsa o'ylab topmagan; biz esa xudoyimizga — Yagona Davlatga sokin, oqilona, puxta o'ylangan qurbonlik keltiramiz.

paras.en: Yes, it was a solemn liturgy for the United State, a reminiscence of the great days, years, of the Two Hundred Years’ War⁠—a magnificent celebration of the victory of all over one, of the sum over the individual!
paras.uz: Ha, bu Yagona Davlat uchun tantanali ibodat edi, Ikki Yuz Yillik Urushning buyuk kunlari, yillari xotirasi — hammaning bittasi ustidan, yig'indining shaxs ustidan g'alabasining ulug'vor bayrami!

paras.en: That one stood on the steps of the Cube which was filled with sunlight. A white, no not even white, but already colorless glass face, lips of glass. And only the eyes⁠—thirsty, swallowing, black holes leading into that dreadful world from which he was only a few minutes away. The golden badge with the number already had been taken off. His hands were tied with a red ribbon. (A symbol of ancient custom. The explanation of it is that in the old times when this sort of thing was not done in the name of the United State, the convicted naturally considered that they had the right to resist, hence their hands were usually bound with chains.)
paras.uz: O'sha bittasi quyosh nuriga to'lgan Kubning zinapoyalarida turardi. Oq, yo'q, hatto oq ham emas, balki allaqachon rangsiz shisha yuz, shisha lablar. Faqat ko'zlar — chanqoq, yutuvchi, u bir necha daqiqa narida bo'lgan o'sha dahshatli dunyoga olib boradigan qora tuynuklar. Raqamli oltin nishon allaqachon olib tashlangan edi. Qo'llari qizil lenta bilan bog'langan edi. (Qadimiy odat ramzi. Uning izohi shundaki, qadimda bunday ish Yagona Davlat nomidan qilinmagan paytlarda, mahkumlar tabiiy ravishda qarshilik ko'rsatishga haqli deb hisoblashgan, shuning uchun ularning qo'llari odatda zanjir bilan bog'langan.)

paras.en: On the top of the Cube, next to the Machine, the motionless, metallic figure of him whom we call the Well-Doer. One could not see his face from below. All one could see was that it was bounded by austere, magnificent, square lines. And his hands.⁠ ⁠… Did you ever notice how sometimes in a photograph the hands, if they were too near the camera, come out enormous? They then compel your attention, overshadow everything else. Those hands of his, heavy hands, quiet for the time being, were stony hands⁠—it seemed the knees on which they rested must have had pains to bear their weight.
paras.uz: Kubning tepasida, Mashina yonida biz Homiy deb ataydigan zotning qimirlamas, metall qiyofasi. Pastdan uning yuzini ko'rib bo'lmasdi. Faqat u qattiq, ulug'vor, kvadrat chiziqlar bilan chegaralanganini ko'rish mumkin edi. Qo'llari esa... Hech payqaganmisiz, ba'zan fotosuratda qo'llar, agar ular kameraga juda yaqin bo'lsa, ulkan bo'lib chiqadi? Shunda ular e'tiboringizni o'ziga tortadi, qolgan hamma narsani soyada qoldiradi. Uning o'sha qo'llari, og'ir qo'llari, hozircha sokin, tosh qo'llar edi — ular tayanib turgan tizzalar ularning og'irligini ko'tarishda qiynalayotgan bo'lsa kerak, deb tuyulardi.

paras.en: Suddenly one of those hands rose slowly. A slow cast-iron gesture; obeying the will of the lifted hand, a Number came out on the platform. It was one of the State poets, whose fortunate lot it was to crown our celebration with his verses.
paras.uz: To'satdan o'sha qo'llardan biri sekin ko'tarildi. Sekin, cho'yan imo-ishora; ko'tarilgan qo'lning irodasiga bo'ysunib, minbarga bir Raqam chiqdi. Bu bayramimizni o'z she'rlari bilan toj kiydirish baxtiga muyassar bo'lgan Davlat shoirlaridan biri edi.

paras.en: Divine iambic brass verses thundered over the many stands. They dealt with the man, who, his reason lost and lips like glass, stood on the steps and waited for the logical consequences of his own insane deeds.
paras.uz: Ko'plab tribunalar ustida ilohiy yamb mis she'rlari gumburladi. Ular aqlini yo'qotib, lablari shishadek bo'lib, zinapoyada turgan va o'zining telbalarcha qilmishlarining mantiqiy oqibatlarini kutayotgan odam haqida edi.

paras.en: … A blaze.⁠ ⁠… Buildings were swaying in those iambic lines, and sprinkling upward their liquified golden substance, they broke and fell. The green trees were scorched, their sap slowly ran out and they remained standing like black crosses, like skeletons. Then appeared Prometheus (that meant us).
paras.uz: ...Yong'in... O'sha yamb satrlarida binolar chayqalar va suyuq oltin moddalarini yuqoriga sachratib, sinib qulardi. Yashil daraxtlar kuyib ketardi, shiralari sekin oqib chiqardi va ular qora xochlardek, skeletlardek turib qolardi. Keyin Prometey paydo bo'ldi (bu biz edik).

paras.en:
“… he harnessed fire
With machines and steel
And fettered chaos with Law.⁠ ⁠…”
paras.uz:
«...U olovni mashina va po'latga qo'shdi,
Tartibsizlikni Qonun bilan kishanladi...»

paras.en: The world was renovated; it became like steel⁠—a sun of steel, trees of steel, men of steel. Suddenly an insane man, “Unchained the fire and set it free,” and again the world had perished.⁠ ⁠… Unfortunately I have a bad memory for poetry, but one thing I am sure of: one could not choose more instructive or more beautiful parables.
paras.uz: Dunyo yangilandi; u po'latdek bo'ldi — po'lat quyosh, po'lat daraxtlar, po'lat odamlar. To'satdan bir telba «olovni kishandan bo'shatib, ozod qildi» va dunyo yana halok bo'ldi... Afsuski, she'rlarni yaxshi eslay olmayman, lekin bir narsaga aminman: bundan ibratliroq yoki go'zalroq timsollarni tanlab bo'lmasdi.

paras.en: Another slow, heavy gesture of the cast-iron hand and another poet appeared on the steps of the Cube. I stood up! Impossible! But⁠ ⁠… thick negro lips⁠—it was he. Why did he not tell me that he was to be invested with such high.⁠ ⁠… His lips trembled; they were gray. Oh, I certainly understood; to be face to face with the Well-Doer, face to face with the hosts of Guardians! Yet one should not allow oneself to be so upset.
paras.uz: Cho'yan qo'lning yana bir sekin, og'ir imo-ishorasi va Kub zinapoyalarida yana bir shoir paydo bo'ldi. Men o'rnimdan turib ketdim! Imkonsiz! Lekin... qalin negr lablari — bu u edi. Nega u menga bunday yuksak... topshirilishini aytmadi? Uning lablari titrardi; ular kulrang edi. Oh, men, albatta, tushundim; Homiy bilan yuzma-yuz, Qo'riqchilar qo'shini bilan yuzma-yuz bo'lish! Lekin baribir o'zini bunchalik hayajonga solmaslik kerak.

paras.en: Swift sharp verses like an axe.⁠ ⁠… They told about an unheard-of crime, about sacrilegious poems in which the Well-Doer was called.⁠ ⁠… But no, I do not dare to repeat.⁠ ⁠…
paras.uz: Boltadek tez, o'tkir she'rlar... Ular eshitilmagan jinoyat haqida, Homiy... deb atalgan kufrona she'rlar haqida hikoya qilardi. Lekin yo'q, takrorlashga jur'at etmayman...

paras.en: R-13 was pale when he finished, and looking at no one (I did not expect such bashfulness of him) he descended and sat down. For an infinitesimal fraction of a second I saw right beside him somebody’s face⁠—a sharp, black triangle⁠—and instantly I lost it; my eyes, thousands of eyes, were directed upward toward the Machine. Then⁠—again the superhuman, cast-iron, gesture of the hand.
paras.uz: R-13 tugatganda rangi oqarib ketgan edi va hech kimga qaramay (undan bunday uyatchanlikni kutmagan edim) pastga tushib o'tirdi. Soniyaning cheksiz kichik ulushi davomida uning shundoq yonida kimningdir yuzini — o'tkir, qora uchburchakni ko'rdim — va darhol uni yo'qotdim; mening ko'zlarim, minglab ko'zlar yuqoriga, Mashinaga qaratildi. Keyin — yana qo'lning g'ayriinsoniy, cho'yan imo-ishorasi.

paras.en: Swayed by an unknown wind the criminal moved; one step⁠ ⁠… one more,⁠ ⁠… then the last step in his life. His face was turned to the sky, his head thrown backward⁠—he was on his last.⁠—⁠ ⁠… Heavy, stony like fate, the Well-Doer went around the machine, put his enormous hand on the lever.⁠ ⁠… Not a whisper, not a breath around; all eyes were upon that hand.⁠ ⁠… What crushing, scorching power one must feel to be the tool, to be the resultant of hundreds of thousands of wills! How great his lot!
paras.uz: Noma'lum shamoldan chayqalib, jinoyatchi qimirladi; bir qadam... yana bir... keyin hayotidagi oxirgi qadam. Yuzi osmonga qaratilgan, boshi orqaga tashlangan edi — u o'zining oxirgi... Og'ir, taqdirdek tosh Homiy mashinani aylanib o'tdi, ulkan qo'lini richagga qo'ydi... Atrofda na pichirlash, na nafas; hamma ko'zlar o'sha qo'lda edi... Yuz minglab irodalarning quroli, natijasi bo'lish qanday ezuvchi, kuydiruvchi qudratni his qilish bo'lsa kerak! Uning taqdiri qanchalik buyuk!

paras.en: Another second. The hand moved down, switching in the current. The lightning-sharp blade of the electric ray.⁠ ⁠… A faint crack like a shiver, in the tubes of the Machine.⁠ ⁠… The prone body, covered with a light phosphorescent smoke; then suddenly, under the eyes of all, it began to melt⁠—to melt, to dissolve with terrible speed. And then nothing; just a pool of chemically pure water which only a moment ago was so red and pulsated in his heart.⁠ ⁠…
paras.uz: Yana bir soniya. Qo'l pastga harakatlanib, tokni ulab yubordi. Elektr nurining chaqmoqdek o'tkir tig'i... Mashina quvurlarida titroqdek zaif chirsillash... Yengil fosforli tutun bilan qoplangan cho'zilgan tana; keyin to'satdan, hammaning ko'z oldida u erib ketdi — erib, dahshatli tezlik bilan eriy boshladi. Keyin hech narsa; faqat bir lahza oldin shunchalik qizil bo'lgan va uning yuragida urib turgan kimyoviy toza suv ko'lmagi...

paras.en: All this was simple; all of us were familiar with the phenomenon, dissociation of matter⁠—yes, the splitting of the atoms of the human body! Yet every time we witnessed it, it seemed a miracle; it was a symbol of the superhuman power of the Well-Doer.
paras.uz: Bularning hammasi oddiy edi; hammamiz bu hodisani — materiyaning dissotsiatsiyasini bilardik — ha, inson tanasi atomlarining parchalanishini! Shunga qaramay, har safar biz unga guvoh bo'lganimizda, bu mo'jizadek tuyulardi; bu Homiyning g'ayriinsoniy qudratining ramzi edi.

paras.en: Above, in front of Him, the burning faces of the female numbers, mouths half open from emotion, flowers swaying in the wind.2 According to custom, ten women were covering with flowers the unif of the Well-Doer, which was still wet with spray. With the magnificent step of a supreme priest He slowly descended, slowly passed between the rows of stands; and like tender white branches there rose toward Him the arms of the women; and, millions like one, our tempestuous cheers! Then cheers in honor of the Guardians, who all unseen, were present among us.⁠ ⁠… Who knows, perhaps the fancy of the ancient man foresaw them centuries ahead, when he created the gentle and formidable “guardian-angels” assigned to each one from the day of his birth?
paras.uz: Yuqorida, Uning oldida, ayol-Raqamlarning yonayotgan yuzlari, hayajondan yarim ochiq og'izlar, shamolda chayqalayotgan gullar. Odatga ko'ra, o'nta ayol Homiyning hali ham sachratqidan ho'l yunifasini gullar bilan qoplardi. Oliy kohinning ulug'vor qadami bilan U sekin pastga tushdi, tribunalar qatorlari orasidan sekin o'tdi; Unga qarab ayollarning qo'llari nozik oq shoxlardek ko'tarildi; va millionlab bir kishidek, bizning bo'ronli olqishlarimiz! Keyin hammasi ko'rinmas holda oramizda hozir bo'lgan Qo'riqchilar sharafiga olqishlar... Kim biladi, ehtimol, qadimgi insonning tasavvuri har bir kishiga tug'ilgan kunidan biriktirilgan muloyim va dahshatli «qo'riqchi farishtalar»ni yaratganda ularni asrlar oldin oldindan ko'rgandir?

paras.en: Yes, there was in our celebration something of the ancient religions, something purifying like a storm.⁠ ⁠… You whose lot it may be to read this, are you familiar with such emotions? I am sorry for you if you are not.
paras.uz: Ha, bizning bayramimizda qadimiy dinlardan nimadir, bo'rondek poklovchi nimadir bor edi... Buni o'qish nasib etishi mumkin bo'lgan siz, bunday tuyg'ularni bilasizmi? Agar bilmasangiz, sizga achinaman.
